newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indocement forecasts good profits in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Indocement forecasts good profits in 1997.

text.p: Indonesian cement maker PT Indocement Tunggal Prakarsa of conglomerate Salim Group on Monday predicted good profits in 1997 due to expansion in cement output.

Indocement president director Sudwikatmono said in a statement the company's expanding cement operations and sales from its food company Indofood, Indonesia's largest noodle maker, should underpin strong recurring profits.

"We expect 1997 will be another excellent year for the group, particularly with the commencement of our 10th cement plant last December which will continue to increase our revenue from cement, along with continuous sales increase from Indofood," Sudwikatmono said.
The new cement plant has a capacity of 1.3 million tonnes a year.
On Monday, PT Indocement Tunggal Prakarsa announced it booked a net profit of 551.49 billion rupiah in 1996. Analysts said the market consensus for the figure had been 549.4 billion rupiah.

Sudwikatmono said the firm will continue to strive for growth and higher levels of performance and profitability in the future with construction of another cement plant to increase the group's annual cement capacity to 15.8 million tonnes by 1999.
He also said the company recognised that proposed Indofood acquisitions provided a good fit for Indofood's operations and should enhance shareholder value.

Indofood said in March it planned to acquire 80 percent equity in six Salim Group companies covering edible oils and fats, oil palm plantations and consumer product distribution operations for a total price of 1.55 trillion rupiah.
